blocks.title: Logistic regression
blocks.text: Logistic regression predicts an outcome that is yes or no. Instead of an exact number, it gives a probability between 0 and 1: P = 1 / (1 + e^-(b0 + b1 x)), where e is the base of natural logarithms, b0 the intercept (log-odds when x = 0) and b1 how much the log-odds change per unit of x.

A predicted probability of 0.85 means an 85% chance of passing. Suppose b0 = 1 and b1 = 0.6: for each hour studied the likelihood of passing increases. A student who studies for 5 hours has P(Pass) = 1 / (1 + e^-(1 + 0.6 x 5)), about 0.83, an 83% chance of passing. For a new student who studies for 4 hours, P(Pass) = 1 / (1 + e^-(1 + 0.6 x 4)), about 0.73, a 73% chance of passing.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: With b0 = 1 and b1 = 0.6 the book's values are wrong. For 5 hours, 1 + 0.6 x 5 = 4 and P = 1 / (1 + e^-4), about 0.98 (a 98% chance); for 4 hours, 1 + 0.6 x 4 = 3.4 and P is about 0.97 (97%). The book's 0.83 and 0.73 are the values for 1 hour and 0 hours.
